extracted.intended_audience: U.S. federal agency staff, policymakers, and contractors implementing the Executive Order on AI (AI governance, procurement, risk management, and related federal programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist/rubric-style summary of the Executive Order's implementation requirements and expectations for government agencies, contractors, and companies developing foundation models. Focuses on risk management, reporting, governance, procurement, safety, privacy, standards, and workforce development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based, government-wide approach to AI governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order's approach is a 'coordinated, risk-based, government-wide approach' rather than blanket prohibition or pure self-regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize coordinated, risk-based oversight across agencies; prioritize sectors, uses, and systems based on potential harms and rights/safety impacts (see summary: 'Coordinated, risk-based, government-wide approach').

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct AI risk assessments (including red‑teaming and post‑deployment monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a risk management practice, agencies are required to conduct assessments for AI systems, including red-team testing and post-deployment performance monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess limitations, vulnerabilities, and harmful behaviors; include pre-deployment testing and continuous monitoring after deployment (references: 'As a risk management practice, the order requires agencies to conduct what type or types of assessment for AI systems?', 'post-deployment performance monitoring').

rubrics_metrics.name: Red‑team testing for dual‑use foundation models
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies developing potential dual‑use foundation models must perform and report red-team testing addressing a set of AI threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report red-team testing results for threats such as accelerating biological weapon development, discovery of software vulnerabilities, self-replication, removal of safeguards, and other misuse scenarios (see items: 'Lowering barrier for biological weapons', 'Discovery of software vulnerabilities', 'Possibility of self‑replication', 'Removal of model safeguards').

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and report 'reportable' AI systems and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order directs agencies/Commerce to define reportable AI systems and require reporting of system characteristics and metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reportable metrics include model scale (number of parameters), computing power used for training, training data sources, and other indicators of system capability/scale (see: 'The order establishes conditions for reportable AI systems involving what metrics? Number of parameters in the model; Amount of computing power used for training; AI system training data sources').

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded agency AI use‑case reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must report expanded information about AI use cases, including purpose, function, risk, mitigation, status, budget, and personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required reporting items include: description of AI system's purpose and function; whether system is deployed or under development; reporting on risks and mitigation measures; estimated budget and personnel resources required (see: 'Description of the AI system's purpose and function', 'Whether system is deployed or under development', 'Reporting on risks and mitigation measures', 'Estimated budget and personnel resources required').

rubrics_metrics.name: Make government data available for AI in machine‑readable, privacy‑preserving formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Government data used in AI training must be accessible in machine‑readable formats and handled to protect privacy and provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data should be 'available in machine-readable formats' and managed to enable provenance tracking while protecting PII (see: 'The order requires all government data used in AI training to have what property? Available in machine-readable formats' and references to stripping PII/provenance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy‑enhancing technologies (PETs) and differential privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and implement privacy‑enhancing technologies to manage privacy risks in AI development and deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PETs such as differential privacy, other techniques to prevent improper data collection/use, and minimize identifiability in training data (see: 'Implementing differential privacy techniques for all data', 'protect against improper data collection and use').

rubrics_metrics.name: Appoint Chief AI and governance roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required or encouraged to appoint senior AI governance roles (e.g., Chief AI Ethics Officer, Chief AI Safety and Security Officer, Chief AI Talent Officer) and establish governance bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roles and bodies include Chief AI Officers Council, Chief Data Officers Council, AI Governance Boards within agencies, and Chief AI Ethics Officers to coordinate activities, provide oversight, and manage accountability (see lists of officer titles and 'The purpose of the Artificial Intelligence Governance Board: To coordinate AI activities across the agency').

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Artificial Intelligence Governance Boards and oversight structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Create governance bodies inside agencies to coordinate AI activities and provide ethical/oversight functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governance Boards should provide ethical oversight, coordinate agency AI activities, and ensure processes for human review and redress (see: 'The purpose of the Artificial Intelligence Governance Board... To provide ethical oversight of AI systems', 'To coordinate AI activities across the agency').

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide human review and avenues for redress
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must provide processes for human review of AI decisions and avenues for redress of adverse AI decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanisms enabling affected individuals to challenge or seek remedy for automated decisions; incorporate human-in-the-loop controls where appropriate (see: 'Providing avenues for redress of adverse AI decisions', 'Processes for human review of AI decisions').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize safety and security in critical sectors (healthcare, critical infrastructure, benefits administration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special safety and oversight requirements are established for AI uses in healthcare, critical infrastructure, and benefits/eligibility determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Healthcare: pre‑market assessment and post‑market oversight of algorithmic performance, incident sharing on patient harms; critical infrastructure: incident response playbooks and monitoring; benefits administration: plans must address effect on access for eligible beneficiaries and include required elements (see multiple references: FDA/NIST/HHS/CISA roles, 'AI safety monitoring program for healthcare entities', 'Methods for assigning liability in AI accidents').

rubrics_metrics.name: NIST guidelines for AI evaluation (adversarial resistance, interpretability, robustness)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIST is directed to develop guidelines to evaluate adversarial attack resistance, model interpretability/explainability, and other robustness characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should include adversarial robustness testing, interpretability/explainability standards, and technical measures to assess resistance to manipulation (see: 'The order directs NIST to develop guidelines to evaluate what type of AI technology? Adversarial attack resistance', 'Model interpretability and explainability').

rubrics_metrics.name: AI red‑teaming guidelines aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The red‑teaming guidance's key goal is to assess limitations, vulnerabilities, and harmful behaviors of AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Red-team exercises should probe safety, misuse modes, robustness, and potential harms; guidance to be issued on how to structure red-team tests (see: 'Assess limitations, vulnerabilities, and harmful behaviors' and related citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop AI incident reporting and response playbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must develop playbooks for AI incident response (particularly for critical infrastructure and healthcare) and capture incidents of harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create interagency incident playbooks, reporting channels, and sharing of incident data; include tracking and capture of patient harms and other AI-induced incidents (see: 'develop an AI incident response playbook for critical infrastructure', 'Identifying and capturing incidents of patient harm deriving from AI').

rubrics_metrics.name: Create government AI testbeds and shared research infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Create government AI testbeds and shared computing/data infrastructure (National AI Research Resource) to enable safe experimentation and research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testbeds aim to provide shared computing and data infrastructure for AI research, enable agencies to test AI solutions pre‑procurement, and support reproducible research (see: 'National AI Research Resource Task Force pilot program... create a shared computing and data infrastructure for AI research', 'government AI testbeds to enable agencies to test AI solutions pre-procurement').

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards development and international engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with standards development organizations and international allies to develop common AI technical standards outside military/intelligence use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce/OSTP to coordinate with standards bodies, allied governments, and international partners on transparency, explainability, and safety standards (see: 'Department of Commerce to engage with... Standards development organizations; Key international allies').

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect civil rights and mitigate algorithmic discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order emphasizes preventing algorithmic discrimination, protecting civil rights, and ensuring equitable outcomes in AI deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include impact assessments for equity, analysis of AI impact on equal access/outcomes, and coordination with FTC/DOJ/Civil Rights Division (see: 'Civil rights and discrimination', 'Mitigating risks of bias and discrimination').

rubrics_metrics.name: Data provenance, labeling, and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and document training data sources, provenance, and data management best practices for AI models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices include data labeling and annotation standards, ability to trace provenance back to original sources, and documentation of data sources used for training (see: 'Data sources used for training models', 'Ability to track the provenance of data back to its original sources', 'Data labeling and annotation best practices').

rubrics_metrics.name: Watermarking and detection of synthetic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Require or encourage watermarking of synthetic content and development of techniques to detect synthetic content and prevent harmful outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop standards for watermarking generative outputs and tools/methods for detecting synthetic content and hallucinations (see: 'Watermarking synthetic content', 'Techniques for detecting synthetic content', 'Preventing hallucinations').

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect workers from AI‑related harms
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop guidance and policies to protect workers from harms such as unfair evaluation, surveillance, pay/compensation issues, and displacement risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secretary of Labor and related agencies to issue guidance to protect workers (e.g., preventing unfair or biased evaluation of job applicants, undue worker surveillance), propose workforce training data rights and privacy principles, and consider labor-market implications (see: 'Guidance from the Secretary of Labor is meant to protect workers from what type of harm?', 'Not being fairly compensated for hours worked', 'Unfair or biased evaluation of job applicants').

rubrics_metrics.name: AI workforce development, hiring, and compensation incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct actions to expand AI talent in government including training resources, internships, pay incentives, and position description libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions include expanding pay incentives, creating internships and recruitment fairs, developing AI career paths and training resources focused on policy/legal/oversight issues, and establishing a position description library for data scientists (see: 'Expand existing pay incentives to hire AI talent', 'Create internships positions for AI', 'position description library for data scientists').

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement guidance and centralization for AI acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify Federal acquisition guidance to centralize and streamline AI acquisition, facilitate access to government-wide acquisition solutions, and prioritize AI-assurance systems when granting authorizations to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GSA and acquisition councils to provide government-wide acquisition solutions, catalogs, and guidance; prioritize systems targeted at AI assurance in authorization processes (see: 'Facilitate access to government-wide acquisition solutions', 'In granting authorizations to operate IT systems, agencies are to prioritize: Systems targeted at AI assurance').

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑market assessment and post‑market oversight for AI in healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: For healthcare AI, the Order focuses on pre-market assessment and post-market oversight of algorithmic performance, patient safety monitoring, and sharing of harms data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop healthcare-specific AI safety monitoring programs, incident reporting/sharing mechanisms, and standards for pre- and post-market performance monitoring (see: 'A key consideration in regulating AI-enabled healthcare technology: Pre-market assessment and post-market oversight of algorithmic performance', 'AI safety monitoring program for healthcare entities').

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and disclosure of AI system details
rubrics_metrics.description: Require disclosure where appropriate of system design, training data sources, and relevant system characteristics to support oversight and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure may include public descriptions of system design, training data sources, training compute/parameters where reportable, and other metadata to enable oversight and public input (see: 'Requiring disclosure of AI training data sources', 'Publicly disclosing AI system design and training data').

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and tools focus for generative AI (safety, hallucination, CSAM prevention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop standards and tools to prevent harmful generative AI outputs (e.g., CSAM), reduce hallucinations, and detect synthetic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST and other agencies tasked to produce tools and standards for detection/prevention (see: 'Preventing generation of child sexual abuse material', 'Preventing hallucinations', 'Techniques for detecting synthetic content').

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and track AI system performance, accuracy, and interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess system performance and accuracy; ensure interoperability with legacy systems and optimize computational efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include user acceptance testing, data labeling best practices, computational efficiency optimization, and measures for interoperability with legacy infrastructure (see: 'Assessing system performance and accuracy', 'Ensuring interoperability with legacy systems', 'Optimizing computational efficiency and speed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect privacy, ensure lawful collection/use/retention of personal data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure collection, use, and retention of personal data for AI is lawful and that privacy is preserved through technical and policy tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce lawful data practices, use PETs, and consider prohibitions or limits on data collection where necessary to protect rights (see: 'The order directs agencies to use policy and technical tools for what purpose related to privacy?', 'To protect against improper data collection and use').

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop AI safety and security boards/committees in Executive Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish boards (e.g., Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Board) within the Executive Office to provide cross-cutting advice on AI safety/security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards provide advice on assessing potential AI risks and mitigation (see: 'What is the primary purpose of the Artificial Intelligence Safety and Security Board? To evaluate potential AI risks and mitigate vulnerabilities').

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase public participation and transparency in AI policymaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit public input and feedback on AI policies and provide avenues for public engagement in agency AI activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public notices, solicit comments, disclose relevant system info for public input, and host public platforms for feedback (see: 'The order highlights the importance of public participation and engagement in agency AI activities through what means? Soliciting public input and feedback on AI policies').

rubrics_metrics.name: Report annually to OMB on AI adoption, incidents, and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to report to OMB annually on AI adoption metrics, incidents of harm/discrimination, budgets, and staffing related to AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus reporting on incidents of harm/discrimination caused by AI, number of AI systems deployed, AI project budgets and expenditures, and staffing/hiring needs (see: 'The order requires agencies to report what to the Director of OMB annually? Incidents of harm or discrimination caused by AI; Number of AI systems deployed; AI project budgets and expenditures').

rubrics_metrics.name: Build standards for nucleic acid screening and biosecurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop specifications and frameworks for nucleic acid synthesis procurement screening and address biosecurity risks from AI-assisted biotechnologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department of Commerce and relevant agencies to define screening specifications, establish research agendas on biosecurity, and create databases/guidance for AI and biosecurity (see: 'The order directs the creation of what, related to biosecurity and AI? Database of AI-assisted biosecurity incidents; Interagency task force on AI and biosafety').

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage safer availability and use of dual‑use AI (risk‑mitigating disclosure and reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require/encourage developers of powerful or dual‑use models to provide ongoing information, risk disclosures, and to participate in mitigation efforts with the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage notifying government about planned activities related to model training, red-team testing results, and participation in standards and safety programs (see: 'What is the stated purpose of reporting by companies developing dual-use foundation models? To provide ongoing information to the government', 'Planned activities related to AI foundation model training').
